children: TORONTO, Nov. 16, 2026 /CNW/ -- H&R Real Estate Investment Trust ("H&R" or "the REIT") (TSX: HR.UN) is pleased to announce its financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026.
NEXT STEPS TO DRIVE UNITHOLDER VALUE AND GOVERNANCE ENHANCEMENTS

On August 11, 2026, the REIT announced that it had entered into an arrangement agreement (the "Arrangement Agreement") with GO Residential Real Estate Investment Trust ("GO REIT") and 1001700058 Ontario Inc. ("Purchaser"), on behalf of a consortium of co-purchasers (which includes funds affiliated with Blackstone Real Estate, Crestpoint Real Estate Investments Ltd., the Public Sector Pension Investment Board and a company controlled by members of the family of Tom Hofstedter, Executive Chairman and CEO of the REIT ("CRAL") (collectively, the "Asset Purchasers"), pursuant to which GO REIT and the Purchaser (on behalf of the Asset Purchasers) agreed to acquire all of the assets of H&R by way of a court-approved plan of arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) in a cash and unit transaction valued at approximately $6.7 billion, including the assumption of certain debt (the "Arrangement Transaction").

On November 13, 2026, the REIT held its unitholder meeting to consider and vote on the Arrangement Transaction. The Arrangement Transaction did not receive the requisite unitholder approval to proceed and accordingly, immediately following the meeting, the REIT terminated the Arrangement Agreement, which resulted in termination of the arrangements with the Asset Purchasers.

Also effective November 13, 2026, the REIT's subsidiaries and and the REDT (as defined below) agreed to terminate the acquisition agreement among them that would have resulted in the REIT indirectly acquiring the remaining interests in the REDT JV LP that it did not already own, in light of the unitholder vote on the Arrangement Transaction.

As a result of the termination of the Arrangement Agreement, the REIT announced the reinstatement of monthly distributions along with a catch-up distribution to compensate for the months of August, September and October 2026, an intention to declare a special cash distribution of approximately $2.30 per Unit prior to the end of 2026 subject to lender approval (in addition to monthly distributions) and an intention to pursue opportunities to surface value for the REIT.

In addition, H&R announced a board refreshment process, with the mandate of the fresh Board of Trustees including a focus on CEO succession planning to ensure that H&R has the leadership in place to execute on its strategy.

Following termination of the Arrangement Transaction after unitholders of the REIT did not approve the Arrangement Transaction, GO REIT commenced an action by Statement of Claim issued on November 13, 2026 in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice against H&R, its trustees and others. The claim seeks a termination fee of approximately $102.1 million and other relief, alleging breaches of the Arrangement Agreement. The Arrangement Agreement was terminated after H&R unitholders did not approve the proposed arrangement at the special meeting of unitholders held on November 13, 2026. The REIT believes the claim is without merit and intends to defend itself vigorously. The REIT's position is that it complied with its obligations under the Arrangement Agreement and that no termination fee is payable to GO REIT or any other member of the consortium of purchasers under the terms of the Arrangement Agreement. The allegations in the Statement of Claim have not been proven in court.

Realty taxes in accordance with IFRS Interpretations Committee Interpretation 21, Levies ("IFRIC 21") relates to the timing of the liability recognition for U.S. realty taxes. By excluding the impact of IFRIC 21, U.S. realty tax expenses are evenly matched with realty tax recoveries received from tenants throughout the period.

Same-Property net operating income (cash basis) decreased by $1.0 million and $6.4 million, respectively, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the respective 2025 periods, mainly resulting from H&R's office segment, primarily due to the expiration of Royal Bank of Canada's lease for 188,526 square feet at 330 Front Street West, in Toronto, ON on December 31, 2025, partially offset by contractual rental escalations at a U.S. office property.

Straight-lining of contractual rent at the REIT's proportionate share decreased by $52.9 million and $69.7 million, respectively, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the respective 2025 periods, primarily due to H&R recording a non-cash adjustment to straight-lining of contractual rent in Q3 2026, in accordance with IFRS 16,

("IFRS 16"), of ($47.3) million to write off the remaining accrued rent receivable relating to the termination of Bell Canada's lease at 200 Bouchard Boulevard, Montreal, QC ("200 Bouchard") in August 2026. In addition, straight-lining of contractual rent at the REIT's proportionate share further decreased for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the respective 2025 period due to a non-cash adjustment to straight-lining of contractual rent of ($15.7) million, relating to the 200 Bouchard First Lease Termination Payment (as defined in the "

Net operating income per the REIT's Financial Statements decreased by $22.5 million and $46.4 million, respectively, for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the respective 2025 periods, primarily due to the sale of $1.7 billion of real estate assets completed during the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

During the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, H&R recorded fair value adjustments on real estate assets as a result of following the REIT's regular internal valuation process. The outcome of this process was then considered in connection with the Arrangement Transaction and in conjunction with a financial fairness opinion received from CIBC World Markets Inc. as well as a financial fairness opinion and formal valuation received from National Bank of Canada Capital Markets, which were both provided to H&R's Board of Trustees.

The largest adjustments recorded were in the residential segment given the continued market softness and lingering supply pressure in the multi-family space whereby H&R increased its weighted average capitalization rate by 30 basis points as well as revised its valuation assumptions to reflect higher rent concessions. Furthermore, rising U.S. Treasury yields has also created downward pressure on valuations given the increase in borrowing costs. This has also put downward pressure on H&R's land parcels held for future development in the United States.

The adjustments made within the industrial segment reflect valuation adjustments based on the contractual sales price approach given that as at September 30, 2026, there was an agreement of purchase and sale for cash consideration. Management views such values to be representative of an orderly transaction between market participants. These adjustments take in account leasing uncertainty, vacancy risk and the potential implications of the ongoing trade tensions between Canada and United States.

Fair value adjustments were made to certain office properties to reflect increased leasing uncertainty and vacancy risk. H&R's largest office property by fair value and square footage is Two Gotham Center in Long Island City, NY. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene occupies 660,431 square feet with their lease expiring in 2030. The leasing risk at the property was incorporated into the future cash flow assumptions in the discounted cash flow model.

During the three months ended September 30, 2026, H&R sold one wholly-owned office property, a 98.5% interest in one office property and a 50% interest in three industrial properties for approximately $168.2 million. In addition, H&R sold its 31.7% interest in one residential property within equity accounted investments for approximately $37.0 million.

In October 2026, H&R sold its remaining industrial lands held for development in Caledon, ON (the "Caledon Lands"), which were classified as held for sale as at September 30, 2026 for $436.0 million. A portion of the proceeds were used to repay one mortgage totalling approximately $125.8 million, as well as all remaining outstanding amounts drawn on H&R's revolving unsecured operating lines of credit totaling $46.0 million.

H&R continues to successfully execute on its strategic repositioning plan with assets sold and under contract to be sold totalling approximately $2.3 billion at the REIT's proportionate share (a non-GAAP measure, refer to the
section of this news release), for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

H&R previously announced in Q3 2022 that it had entered into a lease amendment with Bell Canada to terminate their lease at 200 Bouchard in December 2026, which would have otherwise expired in April 2036. As part of this lease amendment, H&R received a lease termination payment of $15.7 million in April 2026 ("200 Bouchard First Lease Termination Payment"), and was scheduled to receive a second lease termination payment of $55.0 million in December 2026, for a total of $70.7 million. In July 2026, the 200 Bouchard lease was further amended to accelerate the lease termination date to August 2026, which resulted in H&R receiving the final lease termination payment ("200 Bouchard Second Lease Termination Payment") of $56.1 million. As a result of the 200 Bouchard Second Lease Termination Payment, in Q3 2026, H&R recorded a non-cash adjustment to straight-lining of contractual rent of ($47.3) million to write off the remaining accrued rent receivable. Accordingly, 200 Bouchard contributed $9.3 million and $20.0 million, respectively, to net operating income and FFO for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, which included base rent for July 2026. Furthermore, 200 Bouchard contributed $56.6 million and $75.5 million, respectively, to AFFO for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Net operating income from 200 Bouchard has been classified as Transactions (as defined below) and has not been included in Same-Property net operating income. FFO and AFFO are non-GAAP measures. On July 15, 2026, H&R terminated the lease of Coast Appliances Inc. ("Coast") at 140 Speirs Giffen Ave., in Caledon, ON, a single-tenant industrial property totalling 77,754 square feet, in connection with Coast filing for protection from their creditors under the

(Canada) on April 17, 2026. H&R recorded an adjustment to straight-lining of contractual rent of approximately ($0.8 million) in order to write-off the remaining accrued rent receivable as Coast's lease was originally set to expire in November 2032.

In Q3 2026, H&R completed a 5-year lease extension with the Toronto-Dominion Bank whose lease was originally scheduled to expire in November 2027, for 263,448 square feet at 310-320-330 Front St. W., an office property in Toronto, ON.

In Q3 2026, H&R completed a new 3-year direct lease with the existing sub-tenant for 89,405 square feet at a single-tenanted office property in Peterborough, ON. The existing tenant's lease expired in July 2026.

In Q3 2026, H&R completed a new lease for 49,762 square feet at H&R's 50.0% ownership interest at a multi-tenanted industrial property in Toronto, ON, commencing in February 2027 for a 10-year term. The tenant has a 3-month rent free period commencing at the start of the lease term.

In September 2026, H&R transferred 200 Bouchard from investment properties within the office segment to properties under development within the residential segment. H&R plans to demolish the existing building in 2027. The redevelopment plan for the property includes 131 townhome units and 811 multi-residential units across six mid-rise buildings.

H&R has a 29.1% ownership interest in Lantower Residential REDT (No.1) JV LP ("REDT JV LP"). The REDT JV LP owns two residential development projects (the "REDT Projects") in Florida, consisting of 601 residential rental units which were substantially completed and transferred from properties under development to investment properties in Q3 2026. As at September 30, 2026, H&R's share of the total budget for the REDT Projects was approximately $86.6 million (U.S. $61.0 million) with costs remaining to complete of $3.7 million (U.S. $2.6 million), all at H&R's ownership interest, with the REDT projects expected to be completed on budget.

H&R paid its regular monthly distribution for July 2026 in August 2026 as scheduled. On November 13, 2026, the REIT declared a distribution of $0.20 per Unit, consisting of: (i) the reinstatement of the monthly distribution of $0.05 per Unit for the month of November 2026, and (ii) a further $0.15 per Unit to compensate for the months of August, September and October 2026 during which time distributions were suspended pursuant to the Arrangement Agreement. This $0.20 per Unit distribution is payable on December 15, 2026 to unitholders of record on November 30, 2026. The REIT also announced an intention to declare a special cash distribution of approximately $2.30 per Unit prior to the end of 2026, subject to lender approval, in addition to the $0.20 per Unit distribution.

Subsequent to September 30, 2026, H&R repaid one mortgage totalling approximately $125.8 million, which bore interest at 3.67% per annum, using proceeds from the sale of the Caledon Lands. The mortgage was originally scheduled to mature in March 2027 and the early repayment was not subject to any prepayment penalty.
Revolving Unsecured Operating Lines of Credit

Subsequent to September 30, 2026, H&R repaid all remaining outstanding amounts drawn on its revolving unsecured operating lines of credit totaling $46.0 million, using proceeds from the sale of the Caledon Lands.

As at September 30, 2026, H&R had cash and cash equivalents of $82.4 million and $882.1 million available under its unused lines of credit. H&R has an unencumbered property pool of approximately $2.8 billion, which is 3.34x unsecured debt.

As at September 30, 2026, debt to total assets per the REIT's Financial Statements was 32.0% compared to 38.4% as at December 31, 2025. As at September 30, 2026, debt to total assets at the REIT's proportionate share (a non-GAAP ratio, refer to the
section of this news release) was 44.0% compared to 49.8% as at December 31, 2025. Debt to Adjusted EBITDA at the REIT's proportionate share (a non-GAAP ratio,  refer to the

section of this news release) was 6.8x as at September 30, 2026 compared to 9.3x as at December 31, 2025. The improvement in these financial metrics is primarily due to proceeds from property dispositions and lease termination payments being used to repay debt.

H&R published its 2025 Sustainability Report in 2026, highlighting ESG initiatives that exemplify how the REIT's commitment to sustainability is manifesting itself in its portfolio and resulting in lasting changes for its properties, tenants, employees, stakeholders and communities at large.

H&R is pleased to announce that Larry Froom has returned from medical leave and has started to transition back into his role of Chief Financial Officer. Cheryl Fried has acted as Interim Chief Financial Officer from June 1, 2026, providing leadership of the finance and accounting function. H&R thanks Ms. Fried for her contributions during this period. Ms. Fried will return to her role as Executive Vice President, Finance of H&R.
